title: A refused or fragment-quoting flag exempts a footnote's amounts: a rule that drops fn4's +500 sf is kept with no flag
detail: `flagged` (the notes whose amounts a rule may leave out because a flag sends the note to a person) is built from every flag template in the raw answer, before any template is checked. It never looks at whether the flag survived, whether its quote resolved, or which districts it applies in. It also matches by substring (`flat(q['text']) in flat(note['text'])`), so a short fragment such as 'each additional' exempts every note on the page that contains it (fn4 and fn7). Reproduced: the known-bad R-2C template `lot_area >= {area}` (quotes fn4, drops +500 sf per extra occupant) is refused alone. Add one broken flag whose quote is the fragment 'each additional' and is itself refused ('occurs 7 times on chart page 3') and the bad rule is kept: R-2c gets `lot_area >= 2500` and no flag. So a lot for 3 occupants with 2,600 sf passes when the law needs 3,500 sf, and no person is told. This is the exact false pass e6b68a3 says it closes.
evidence: drafter.py:891 `flagged = frozenset((q["page"], n) for t in answer["templates"] if t["kind"] == "flag" for q in t["quotes"] if q.get("document") == "chart" and flat(q.get("text")).strip() for n, note in (notes.get(q.get("page")) or {}).items() if flat(q["text"]) in flat(note["text"]))`; drafter.py:952 `elif dropped := note_amount_problems(t, notes, flagged):`. Scratch test (scratchpad/r10/test_flag.py) output: `ALONE kept []`, `WITH FLAG kept ['R-2c'] ['lot_area >= 2500']`, `flag survived? ['lot_area_one_family_detached_fn4'] ["...broken_flag: chart quote 'each additional' occurs 7 times..."]`
pin: test_gap_templates.py: a new test that judges [dropped-fn4 template, a flag quoting 'each additional' that is refused] and asserts got['rules'] == {} (no R-2c rule without +500). A second case: a flag that survives only in another district (applies_when district == "R-3a") does not exempt R-2c.
suggested_fix: Settle the exemption after the loop, from what was kept. A note counts as flagged for district D only if a flag rule kept for D (in out['rules'][D]) has a resolved source (its `sources`, not the raw quote text) that is that note: same page and the note's own piece or lines, not a substring. Otherwise run note_amount_problems again for that template and district and move the rule to unresolved.

At drafter.py:891-893 (added by e6b68a3; it is not on 0178c8b), `flagged` is built from every `kind == "flag"` template in the raw `answer["templates"]` before the loop at line 894 checks any of them. So it ignores whether the flag is later rejected (template_problems, resolve_quotes and _binding_items at lines 895-911), whether it resolves, and what scope it has. It also matches a quote to a note by substring (`flat(q["text"]) in flat(note["text"])`). At line 952, note_amount_problems(t, notes, flagged) then skips any note in `flagged` (lines 419-420). I ran the reviewer's scratch test (scratchpad/r10/test_flag.py, built on test_gap_templates) against this checkout. The core false-pass path the finding describes is real.

title: A relaxing rule is kept with only some of the exception's conditions, so the chart limit passes designs the law fails
detail: With `relaxes`, an exception's conditions are no longer separate parts that all_or_none can drop together. They are the relaxer's own applies_when, and a match there makes the chart rule PASS. The code checks only that applies_when is non-empty (templates.py:125, the README's 'never kept without its conditions'). Nothing checks that every condition the quoted law sets is there, for example 'each required front, side and rear yard is increased'. Reproduced: a §325-16C bonus template whose applies_when is only `front_yard >= {front} + (building_height - {height})` (side and rear yards left out, quotes and numbers otherwise valid) is kept in all nine districts with no problems. The composed R-1a height rule then returns PASS for a 37 ft house with 1 ft side yards and a 1 ft rear yard. Before relaxes, a missing part could only leave the 35 ft chart rule failing (stricter). Now it is a false pass. The tests cover only an empty applies_when and a wrong slot name, never a partial one.
evidence: templates.py:124-126 `if template["kind"] != "rule" or not template.get("applies_when", "").strip(): p.append("a rule that relaxes another needs its conditions ...")` is the only condition check; rulebook.py:91 `widen = " or ".join(f"(({x['applies_when']}) and ({x['check']}))" ...)`. Scratch test (scratchpad/r10/test_partial.py): `problems []`, `kept ['R-1a', ... 'RU']`, outcome of the composed R-1a.max_height_ft at {building_height 37, front_yard 27, side yards 1, rear_yard 1, lot_depth 100} = `pass`.
pin: test_gap_templates.py: test_a_relaxing_rule_without_its_conditions_or_its_target_is_never_kept gains a case bonus(applies_when=front-only) with its side/rear slots removed, asserting got['rules'] == {} (or that every kept relaxer, applied, FAILs a 37 ft design with chart-minimum side and rear yards).
suggested_fix: Do not let an unapproved (AI-drafted) relaxer turn a fail into a pass. Two options. (1) apply_relaxes composes a draft relaxer as review only: where the base fails and the relaxer's conditions and check hold, the result is needs review, never pass, until the rule is approved (principle 4). (2) An engineer-written list of conditions per exception (for §325-16C: front_yard, side_yard_smaller, side_yard_larger, rear_yard, each with + (building_height - limit)). link_relaxes refuses a relaxer whose applies_when doesn't constrain every one of them, checked by evaluating it at the chart minimums with one yard short.

It requires `relaxes` to name a slot and `applies_when` to be non-empty, and nothing more. link_relaxes (drafter.py:833-853) only finds the target chart rule. The fill/validate path (drafter.py:917-921 and onward) adds no check that applies_when covers every condition in the quoted law. rulebook.py:91 composes the target as `own check OR (relaxer.applies_when AND relaxer.check)`. rulebook.py:194-195 applies that composition every time a zone rulebook is loaded, so the checker does see the widened rule. all_or_none (drafter.py:806-829) protects only exceptions split into several slotted templates that share one applies_when. A single relaxer whose conditions are incomplete never reaches it. I ran the reviewer's scratch test from scratchpad/r10/test_partial.py, copied temporarily into packages/rule_drafting/tests and removed afterwards, using the repo venv on e6b68a3. It printed `problems []`, then `kept ['R-1a', 'R-1b', 'R-2a', 'R-2b', 'R-2c', 'R-3a', 'R-3aa', 'R-3b', 'RU']`, then `pass` for a 37 ft house with 1 ft side and rear yards against the composed R-1a height rule. This path is new in this PR: before `relaxes`, an exception could not widen the chart limit, so a missing part left the result stricter. This breaks the "never a false pass" principle.

1. The only check on a relaxing rule's conditions is templates.py:121-125. It checks that `relaxes` names a slot and that applies_when is not blank. rulebook.py `_relaxes_problems` does the same: it only needs an applies_when to exist.
2. Nothing compares the conditions against what the quoted law requires. link_relaxes (drafter.py:833-853) only finds the target chart rule. 3. all_or_none (drafter.py:805-830) only keeps separate templates together when they share an applies_when. When all the conditions sit in one relaxer's applies_when, it does nothing.

Before this PR, a stand-alone bonus rule missing a condition still left the 35 ft chart rule failing, so the result was stricter, not a false pass. The worked examples are written by the AI, so they don't catch this either.

One caveat: no relaxing rule appears in the drafted R-1a.yaml now committed, so the risk is a path the AI's next draft can hit, not a false pass already in the data. Still, the false-pass path is real, it is new in this PR, and code does not guard it.

title: The composed check nests its ways, so the panel loses the yards the bonus raises and the 'either way' advice
detail: apply_relaxes builds `(base) or (((aw) and (c)))`. Python's ast keeps the parenthesised `and` nested: Or[base, And[And[yard compares], c]]. present._holding_way and present._alternatives only look at the direct Compare children of each alternative. For a relaxes-composed rule they therefore see only `building_height <= 38.5` and miss all four yard comparisons. For the hand combined rule they see all five. Result: _raise_yards never raises the yard rows when the bonus is what passes the height (the yard rows show '+2'-0' to spare when the bonus needs those 2 ft, the very thing that guard exists to stop). And a failing height row's 'Does not comply either way' lists no yard shortfalls. The test's claim that the hand and relaxes versions are equivalent covers outcome() only, not what the panel shows. With several relaxers the widen is a nested Or and _holding_way returns [].
evidence: Ran present._holding_way on the composed rule at h=37 with enlarged yards: relaxed -> ['building_height <= 35 + 0.1 * 35']; hand COMBINED -> [height, front, side, side, rear]. present._alternatives at h=40: relaxed second way [('Building height','40','≤','38.5','2')]; hand second way also lists Front yard 27 ≥ 30, Side yards 12 ≥ 15.
pin: test_relaxes.py: assert present._holding_way(composed['check'], v) and present._alternatives(...) give the same comparisons as for COMBINED on the grid's passing-by-bonus and failing designs.
suggested_fix: Build the composed check flat, as a formula: parse base, each aw and each check, flatten nested And/Or (base or aw_1 and ... and c_1 or ...), and ast.unparse it. Or have present flatten BoolOps of the same op before reading the ways. The first keeps one formula shape for every reader.

Two functions in packages/design_checker/design_checker/present.py only look at the direct Compare children of each way. _holding_way (line 447) uses `getattr(alt, "values", [])` filtered to ast.Compare, and _alternatives (line 386) does the same. The equivalence test in test_relaxes.py only compares outcome(), not the panel. Nothing upstream flattens the nested And. This code is new in this PR, not code that already existed on 0178c8b.

title: link_relaxes picks its target as 'the one rule citing the height cell'; the planned §325-18B eaves rule also cites it, so the bonus is refused everywhere
detail: A target is any drafted rule of the district, from another unit, whose sources cite the slot's cell. The §325-18B eaves template that test_gap_templates accepts as the correct re-draft cites 'Height in feet' (for its review_when 'building_height > {height}'). Once both are drafted, every district has two rules citing the height cell, and link_relaxes refuses the bonus everywhere ('cited by several rules here'). So the height bonus e6b68a3 was built for is never linked after the re-draft it plans. The drafter will also be told to retry (paid calls) for something the AI can't fix.
evidence: `targets = [r for r in drafted.get(district) or [] if r.get("kind") == "rule" and not r.get("relaxes") and not r["id"].startswith(own) and any(x.get("cell") == cell and x.get("page") == slot["page"] for x in r.get("sources") or [])]`; `if len(targets) != 1: return None, ...`. Scratch test (scratchpad/r10/test_amb.py), adding the accepted eaves rules to drafted: `KEPT []`, problems '...the chart rule it widens ('Height in feet') is cited by several rules here...' for R-1a, R-1b, R-2a ...
pin: test_gap_templates.py: judge the eaves template, add its rules to drafted_rules, then judge bonus(): every district keeps the relaxer, linked to `<D>.max_height_ft`.
suggested_fix: Choose the target by what it limits: a rule whose check compares the slot's measure (the relaxer check's left side, building_height) against that cell's number, for example `building_height <= 35`. Not every rule that cites the cell in a review_when or a source.

title: filled_elsewhere drops a gap when a cell's numbers are used, even if the kept rules don't cover every use the failed template covered

title: Chains are not refused; a relaxer that is itself relaxed is widened; a non-text relaxes crashes validate
detail: _relaxes_problems refuses only cycles. Y relaxes X relaxes B validates clean, and apply_relaxes widens X with Y (relaxed_by ['R-1b.y']). That contradicts the README ('the relaxing rule ... is never widened itself') and the intended 'no chains'. B is not widened through Y, so the semantics differ by path. Separately, `relaxes: [x]` makes validate raise TypeError (unhashable list in `target not in ids`) before the 'must be text' check can report it.
evidence: Ran: validate([BASE, BONUS, Y relaxes BONUS]) relax-problems -> []; apply_relaxes(...)[1]['relaxed_by'] -> ['R-1b.y']; validate([BASE, BONUS|{'relaxes': ['x']}]) -> TypeError unhashable type: 'list'.
pin: test_relaxes.py test_relaxes_is_checked_statically: assert a 'chain' problem for [BASE, BONUS, Y], and that a list-valued relaxes gives a problem, not an exception.
suggested_fix: In _relaxes_problems, skip non-str targets (TEXT_FIELDS reports them), and refuse a target that itself has `relaxes` (a chain). In apply_relaxes, never widen a rule that has `relaxes`.
skeptics: I couldn't refute it; all three parts hold, and all of the code involved is new in this diff. (1) In packages/rule_format/rule_format/rulebook.py, _relaxes_problems (lines 100-125) checks for self-relaxing, a target not in this rulebook, a target with no check, a relaxer with no applies_when or check, and cycles (the walk at 119-123).
